stewart_read: The customer raises a trust flag about caller-ID spam labeling almost immediately after the rep's generic form-fill intro. The rep's intro at 00:05 didn't pre-empt this by naming a specific legitimacy anchor beyond 'the solar form you filled out online.'
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could not have prevented a carrier-side spam label regardless of intro quality, so this may be an unavoidable friction point rather than an intro failure.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to have a one-line ready response for spam-flagged numbers (carrier labeling, not company practice) before the customer has to raise it.

quote: Anyway, you know, we had spoke to somebody a long time ago about it.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior solar conversation and, moments later, a no-show from that company. This is a recycled-lead signal (prior touchpoint, possibly bill/design already on file) as well as competitive intel, and the rep does not probe either angle.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be deliberately staying in verify-sequence to avoid derailing momentum, planning to resurface the history later — but no later moment in the transcript shows this follow-up happening.
coaching_implication: Ask the rep to spend 10-15 seconds asking which company and what was promised; this both surfaces recycled-lead status and gives the closer competitive context.

stewart_read: The customer repeats and sharpens the same complaint — paperwork was sent to a prior company and no appointment ever came. The rep again answers 'Okay' and moves to the meter question rather than asking what was actually submitted.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is best-supported here since this is the second occurrence of the same signal with no attempt made either time.
coaching_implication: This is the second touch of the same missed opening — flag as a pattern, not a one-off, in the 1-on-1.

stewart_read: When the customer says he has to take another call, the rep offers an open-ended 'should I call you back' instead of stating a concrete wait time or callback window, and the resulting gap runs from 02:55 to 03:59 — over a minute of dead air on the recording.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have simply been reacting politely in real time with no better option available since the interruption was sudden.
coaching_implication: Coach a tighter holding line ('I'll hang on just a sec' or a specific redial time) to reduce dead-air risk and keep momentum on future calls with mid-call interruptions.

quote: My wife knows all that stuff. She takes care of the bills.
stewart_read: The customer defers bill knowledge to his wife. This is not an explicit request to consult a spouse before deciding, so it reads more as a bill-knowledge gap than a stated co-decider objection — but it is a signal the rep could have used to ask whether the wife should be included on the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: This may simply be an informational aside with no decision-making implication, in which case no protocol was actually triggered.
coaching_implication: Flag as a soft opportunity: when bill-knowledge is deferred to a spouse, it's worth a light follow-up ('should we get her on the call too since she handles the bills?') rather than moving straight past it.

quote: So what does it cost me out of pocket to get it?
stewart_read: Having introduced the 'bill swap' framing unprompted at 06:16, the rep now has to field a direct cost question — content the schema flags as closer-tier. The rep answers with 'no upfront cost out of pocket' rather than redirecting to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's answer stays within the safe, no-numbers script language rather than quoting a price, so this could be read as acceptable value-framing rather than true scope creep.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the escape hatch language ('that's exactly what the specialist walks through with real numbers') so cost questions don't get answered in generalities that could set false expectations.

quote: You still there? Just making sure.
stewart_read: The call ends with no day/time appointment, no button-up recap, and the rep repeatedly calling out into silence before giving up with 'I'll call you right back.' No next step is locked.
alternative_hypothesis: This is a dropped call/technical failure outside the rep's control, not a coaching failure of button-up discipline.
coaching_implication: Note for the manager: this looks like a genuine connection loss, not a scripted failure — but confirm whether a follow-up call/text was actually made after this transcript ends.
